correctness.rationale: Kernel coefficients follow exactly from Beta moments. The inradius proof uses the checked concavity of arg(1+r exp(i delta)) and pr<=1. The Möbius map takes the disk to x>1/2 and its derivative p u^(p-1) is never zero. The boundary critical-point identity Fprime=-p sin((p-1)phi)/cos(phi)^(p+1) proves all crossing counts. The only double boundary roots satisfy cos(phi)=1/2 and (p-1)phi even multiple of pi, hence p=6k+1. Nonzero second and parameter derivatives prove local square-root splitting. Numerical checks supplement, do not replace, the proof.

value.rationale: A canonical continuum of radial harmonic reproducing kernels has a sharp scalar zero-free radius, exact count of every boundary zero for each arbitrary real weight, and an infinite discrete series of quadratic contacts with explicit saddle-node splitting. These are motivated global nodal geometry and degeneracy invariants rather than a single numeric sample or textbook positivity calculation; the derivation distinguishes harmonic kernels from always-zero-free standard holomorphic power kernels.
